issue.title: test: TestLaneLimitRoutes reads the running gateway outside its sandbox
issue.body:
`TestLaneLimitRoutes` assumes `GET /api/lanes` returns `{}` because that test
does not start a gateway. `providerRoutes` intentionally falls back to
`gateway.OwnerLanes()`, however, which can read another running Magpie at the
default loopback address. A temporary HOME does not isolate that endpoint.

Reproduced on unchanged upstream `247794c61`, Go 1.26.8. The same test fails
deterministically against a controlled fixture owner, so this does not depend
on a live user's provider data.

Fixture:

```text
GET /v1/magpie/concurrency
200 {"data":{"fixture-owner":{"busy":3,"waiting":0,"limit":0}}}
```

Run:

```sh
MAGPIE_ADDR=127.0.0.1:<fixture-port> GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 \
  go test -tags nogui ./internal/gui -run '^TestLaneLimitRoutes$' -count=1
```

The test fails at its final empty-lanes assertion with the fixture data.
Pointing it at a non-serving address makes the unchanged test pass.

The test should provide a controlled non-serving owner endpoint, for example
an `httptest` server returning 404, rather than relying on the machine's
default port being unused. Production owner fallback is intentional and does
not need changing. A global test-runner `MAGPIE_ADDR` override is unsuitable:
other agent fixtures make their own fixed-address assertions.

Found during model-catalog verification; no production gateway or user
configuration was changed.

`TestLaneLimitRoutes` now points owner discovery at its own loopback HTTP fixture returning 404. Its empty-lanes assertion is unchanged, and production owner fallback is unchanged. The test therefore no longer reads an unrelated gateway running on the machine.

A controlled owner exposing a nonempty `fixture-owner` lane makes the original test fail with that extra lane; the isolated test passes. A separate real `/api/lanes` Handler test verifies that a console without a local gateway still displays its owner's lanes. Related race tests and owner loopback-boundary checks pass, as do scoped vet/build, formatting and diff checks. I independently reran the three affected tests.

No full suite, cross-platform run or Go 1.26.8 run was performed; validation used Go 1.27.3. AI-assisted implementation and review.

issue.title: agents: preserve upstream model groups and canonical Grok capability IDs

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
When Magpie serves the same upstream catalog to Hermes, DSH and Grok Build,
the model pickers do not retain the same upstream structure and capabilities.
This is reproducible on upstream `247794c613440dcb317ad9a8189c659ec2be8c63`.

- Hermes receives `providers.magpie.models` as model-ID strings. The callable
  IDs survive, but names, upstream groups, contexts and per-model reasoning
  choices are lost.
- Grok registers `magpie/relay/model` while `/v1/models` returns `relay/model`.
  The two identities can appear separately, and reasoning capability metadata
  can attach to the configured alias instead of the model actually selected.
- DSH already retains public IDs through its `magpie`, `magpie-responses` and
  `magpie-anthropic` routes. Its ACP model option groups by those routes, so a
  client needs a small display-only decode of their opaque route/model tuples.

Expected behavior:

1. Export generic Hermes metadata keyed by each unchanged callable ID:
   `name`, `group`, known `context_length`, and explicit `reasoning_efforts`.
   Normalize the catalog's `off` level to Hermes's `none`. Preserve user
   metadata overrides and deletions across refreshes and failed writes.
2. Use one public Grok registration/wire/default ID. Migrate proven managed
   aliases and cached IDs, retain existing sessions and user context windows,
   and refuse collisions with user-owned canonical entries.
3. Preserve DSH's three protocol routes, exact selectors, compatibility
   settings and per-model reasoning mappings.
4. Let ACP clients consume the catalog, with only finite display compensation
   where the agent cannot express source groups.

The implementation is ready in turingcat/magpie#1, with four feature commits
based on upstream `247794c61` and reviewed source tree
`35ba8eb6adbc968276adc5b3a3c41683ebf4b7d3`. Upstream PR creation was attempted
and rejected because turingcat lacks `CreatePullRequest` permission; the fork
PR provides the complete reviewable patch for pickup.

Companion changes: spacering-net/codeg#1093 and
NousResearch/hermes-agent#148733. Native groups and reasoning controls are
implemented in their owning projects, without a hardcoded model/provider
catalog in Codeg.

All feature-scoped regressions and required races pass. macOS/Linux/Windows
vet and builds pass. The final complete Go suite still has three failures
reproduced on unchanged upstream: #5149, #4526 and #5150. Their causes and
controlled reproductions are recorded separately. Real Grok 1.0.70 and DSH
ACP recording-endpoint checks passed, including original IDs and selected
reasoning values. Checks used temporary homes; live agent configurations
and paid model endpoints were not used.

issue.title: [Bug] Codex /models：x-api-key 覆盖有效 OAuth 为 Bearer magpie，导致 401 和上下文回退

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## 问题与影响

Codex 保留 ChatGPT 登录、同时使用 Magpie 的 managed gateway key 时，GET `/backend-api/codex/models` 会返回 401。已用同一份有效 OAuth 做请求对照：只去掉 `x-api-key`，同一路径立即返回 200 和正确的模型窗口。

源码确认：`identifyCaller` 验证 gateway key 后，把原本有效的 `Authorization` 覆盖为内部标记 `Bearer magpie`；模型目录路径随后把这个标记转发给 ChatGPT，没有重新签名。

这会让 Codex 无法刷新 Magpie 声明的模型元数据。本机 Astra 会话的有效窗口实际从 828400 回退到 258400，自动压缩阈值从 784800 降到 244800，长会话随后反复压缩。模型和推理档位仍为 Astra / Ultra。

## 环境与配置

- Magpie **v0.1.2909**，macOS arm64。
- Codex 桌面端内置 CLI **0.166.0-alpha.6**。
- 核查时间：2026-11-04。
- Magpie 的 Codex provider 对 `gpt-6-astra` 显式设置 `contexts = 872000`。
- Codex 没有显式设置 `model_context_window` 或 `model_auto_compact_token_limit`。
- 当前接入配置如下；不主张这段配置一定由 Magpie 自动生成：

```toml
model = "gpt-6-astra"
model_provider = "custom"
model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"

[model_providers.custom]
name = "OpenAI"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/backend-api/codex"
wire_api = "responses"
requires_openai_auth = true
supports_websockets = false

[model_providers.custom.http_headers]
x-api-key = "<valid Magpie managed gateway key>"
```

该 custom provider 没有 `experimental_bearer_token`，也没有额外配置 `Authorization`；OAuth 来自 Codex 已有登录。

## 最小复现：仅查询模型目录

对同一个本机网关发送：

```http
GET /backend-api/codex/models?client_version=0.166.0
Authorization: Bearer <valid Codex OAuth access token>
ChatGPT-Account-ID: <matching account>
x-api-key: <valid Magpie managed gateway key>
Accept: application/json
```

在同一次验证中，仅改变认证头组合：

| 请求头 | 实际结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 有效 OAuth + 对应 account header + 有效 x-api-key | **401** |
| 同一份 OAuth + 同一个 account header，去掉 x-api-key | **200**；Astra 的 context_window 和 max_context_window 均为 **872000** |
| 只有有效 x-api-key | **401**，错误相同 |

401 正文：

```json
{"detail":"Could not parse your authentication token. Please try signing in again."}
```

第二组仍然经过 Magpie，并非绕开网关直连。它说明这一失败不需要 OAuth 失效或重新登录才能触发。验证只发送 GET 模型目录请求，没有为此发送推理请求。

## 源码原因

以下链接固定到安装版本 v0.1.2909：

1. [loopback 请求带 managed key 时进入 identifyCaller](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/lan.go#L493-L503)；[callerKeys / managedKey 包含 x-api-key](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/lan.go#L740-L774)。
2. [identifyCaller 无条件覆盖 Authorization](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/lan.go#L672-L680)：

   ```go
   r.Header = r.Header.Clone()
   r.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+Token)
   ```

   [Token 是公开常量 "magpie"](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/gateway.go#L54)，不是用户的 OAuth。
3. [GET /models 进入 codexModels](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/codex_backend.go#L90-L93)。[askCodexList 复制认证头后直接发送](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/codex_backend.go#L2191-L2206)，[copyHeaders 保留 Authorization](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/codex_backend.go#L2073-L2078)。
4. [普通 401 原样返回，提前退出](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/codex_backend.go#L2225-L2251)，因此后续 [CodexNativeWindow / 窗口覆盖](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2909/internal/gateway/codex_backend.go#L2279-L2294) 没有执行。

核查时 main 为 `3eb2bda4f2e3ba8aa0eb2c7870d9c746798687a1`；上述 `lan.go` 和 `codex_backend.go` 与 v0.1.2909 完整文件内容一致。运行复现基于安装版，main 只做了源码对照。

## 上下文回退的现场证据

同一个 Astra / Ultra 长会话在当天 15:23 前后出现以下运行时值变化（UTC+8，摘录必要字段）：

```text
full_context_window_limit: 828400 -> 258400
auto_compact_scope_limit: 784800 -> 244800
```

Codex 当前安装程序的内置 Astra 目录是 `context_window=272000, max_context_window=872000`；258400 正好是 `272000 × 95%`。正常拿到 Magpie 的 872000 覆盖时，有效窗口为 828400。

同机还出现过缓存过期和 provider/auth identity mismatch，但不是每条都来自受影响会话的进程；不把它们当成这次认证覆盖的必要触发条件，也没有把每次历史窗口跳变都归因于同一原因。

## 期望

同时携带有效 gateway key 和 ChatGPT OAuth 时，gateway key 用于本地身份/权限校验，Codex 原生目录请求应保留或正确恢复其上游 OAuth 身份，不能把内部 `Bearer magpie` 发给 ChatGPT。

建议增加回归用例：在 mock ChatGPT 上游断言“有效 OAuth + managed x-api-key”的模型目录请求仍使用正确 OAuth，且返回列表应用用户的窗口覆盖；同时保留 gateway key 的权限和失效检查。

相关：#1955 是模型目录超时后的旧窗口回退；#4308 是登录确已被撤销。本例的区别是 OAuth 本身有效，加上 managed x-api-key 才触发 401。


另见 #2145：该报告针对 WSL NAT 的远程接入，维护者通过调整接入方式修复且报告者已确认。本例发生在本机回环地址，并用有效 OAuth 与 managed key 的双凭据对照定位到了头部覆盖。

issue.title: provider: opt-in GLM API-key auto-reset on quota exhaustion (scoped patch + live API evidence)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
This delivers a small, provider-key-only auto-reset patch for #2568 and #2716, with a fresh live check of BigModel's API-key authentication. Thanks to @Jichao for the endpoint investigation in #2716; the commit credits that contribution.

### Live evidence (2026-11-05)

Using the personal GLM Coding Plan API key already configured in Magpie, without a ZCode or browser session:

- `GET https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/biz/customer-package-reset/list?targetType=PERSONAL` returned available weekly cards.
- `POST /api/biz/customer-package-reset/use`, with the bare API key in `Authorization` and `{targetType: "PERSONAL", resetType: "WEEK", recordId: <selected ID>, grantType: "GLOBAL", requestId: <UUID>}`, returned `code: 200, success: true`.
- A separate quota read changed five-hour usage **100% → 0%** and weekly usage **69% → 0%**. Available weekly cards changed **3 → 2**.

This was an explicitly authorized manual API call. It verifies the vendor protocol and weekly-card behavior; it is not a live test of the new automatic gateway path. No account IDs, keys or sessions are included here. Z.ai has not been live-tested by this contribution.

### Proposed behavior and patch scope

`magpie provider auto-reset <id> on|off` opts one personal GLM plan key into automatic consumption. Default: off. It follows the exact key and vendor; replacing a key does not inherit consent. The initial command enables single-key providers; disabling remains possible after adding another key.

After every candidate is unavailable and a request receives a quota-exhaustion refusal, the gateway re-reads personal quota, chooses the matching unexpired card with the earliest expiry, consumes it, verifies quota recovery and retries the request. Weekly exhaustion takes priority. A five-hour exhaustion does not automatically spend a more valuable weekly card if no five-hour card exists.

A separate per-key, machine-local state file and cross-process lock protect consumption. The original window deadline, selected record and request ID are written atomically **before** the POST. Uncertain responses, failed writes/reads/locks and restarts cannot turn into another automatic POST during that window. Toggling off/on preserves the reservation. Codex's state and history remain separate.

This patch covers API-key providers. ZCode plugin accounts, team cards, expiry scheduling, peak-hour policy and a GUI settings switch are outside this first patch. The routing story identifies GLM in all supported translations. Automated consumption should be enabled on only one machine for a given key.

### Delivery and verification

Draft PR on my fork: https://github.com/hhh2210/magpie/pull/2

Commit: https://github.com/hhh2210/magpie/commit/8ab06857d82695bcdb077ace24b558a74c7519f2

```sh
git fetch https://github.com/hhh2210/magpie.git feat/glm-key-auto-reset
git cherry-pick 8ab06857d82695bcdb077ace24b558a74c7519f2
```

Based on upstream `435f04151`. Diff: production **+266/-2**, tests **+288/-0**, docs **+39/-0**.

Passed:
- Focused provider, CLI and gateway tests; provider/gateway `-race -count=3` (sandbox HOME/config, pinned Go caches).
- Behavioral regression: disabling the new gateway integration makes `TestGLMAutoResetRequest` fail with HTTP 429 / zero spends / one attempt; restoring it gives HTTP 200 / one spend / successful retry.
- Native, Linux and Windows vet/build; built CLI on/off under synthetic configuration; formatting/diff checks.
- Headless Chromium routing-story checks in English and Chinese, including GLM text. Full provider and CLI packages pass.

Not green / not run:
- Full `go test -tags nogui ./...`: JSON marshal parity failures (#5348, reproduced on unchanged base), gateway package exceeded its 10-minute budget, `TestLaneLimitRoutes` (#5150), `TestPluginSOCKSProxy` (#2207; existing fix branch is tracked there).
- `i18n-keys`: existing #5332 failure (`View routing` in a Go-test comment).
- WebKit, full browser suite and live automatic spending not run. Environment: macOS arm64, Go 1.27.3, Bun 1.4.4.

No production Magpie binary or auto-reset setting was changed.

The live automatic-spend gate requested in #2716 remains open. Please treat this as a **draft for review**, not a claim that all merge gates passed. A real card was already used for the protocol check; no further cards were spent just to generate test evidence.

For integration, please cherry-pick the linked commit with its author retained. If squashing or reimplementing the patch, please preserve `Co-authored-by: hhh2210 <hzy2210@gmail.com>` and the contribution credit already in the commit.

issue.title: gui: manage saved search API keys individually

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Settings › Models › Web search currently replaces an API's saved keys when another key is added, and APIs without quota support do not show a usable list. This change appends new keys and gives each saved key a Providers-style row with Copy, Change key, and individual removal.

Closes yetone/magpie#4597. Refs yetone/magpie#1477.

This is a draft for owner review in the fork. The upstream [contributor policy](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/bd0f3382827e4eedb2478773d5f67107ec0eac0a/docs/contributors.md) limits PRs to collaborators; this account is not an upstream collaborator.

### Behavior

- Saved keys remain editable while quotas load or fail. Usage attaches by fingerprint, even when masks match. Older requests cannot overwrite newer lists, and quota completion preserves an active editor and its focus.
- Existing API order, switches, plugin sign-in, whole-API Show/Copy, and routing remain. An omitted URL preserves the saved endpoint; an explicitly empty URL restores the vendor default.
- CLI parity: `magpie search rm <api> [<n>]` can remove one key. The separate pre-existing `search move` parser defect is tracked in yetone/magpie#5354 ([separate draft](https://github.com/vizmoe/magpie/pull/2)).

- A browser using the real Settings HTTP handler and isolated demonstration data replaced the first Exa key while preserving the second, then appended two keys and confirmed the resulting four-key list through `/api/settings`.

issue.body:
## 需求

希望将“资源库 → 子代理”统一改为“资源库 → 代理”，并在新增、编辑代理时，支持设置该代理作为**主代理**或**子代理**使用。

## 使用场景

自定义代理除了被其他代理调用，也可以作为用户直接对话、发起任务的主代理。希望在资源库中统一管理这些代理，并明确它们的使用角色。

## 期望行为

- 资源库入口及相关页面名称由“子代理”改为“代理”。
- 新增、编辑代理时，可以选择“主代理”或“子代理”。
- 同步到目标客户端时，在客户端支持的范围内，让代理按所选角色生效：主代理可作为用户直接使用的会话入口，子代理可供其他代理调用。
- 对于不支持某种角色的客户端，在界面中明确说明支持范围。
- 已有子代理保留原有配置和用途，升级后默认仍为子代理。

核心是让资源库统一管理代理，并显式设置其角色。具体界面与各客户端的适配方式可由维护者决定。

issue.title: Library: installing a skill from a SHA-256 git repository fails with `mismatched algorithms: client sha1; server sha256`

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
# Library: installing a skill from a SHA-256 git repository fails with `mismatched algorithms: client sha1; server sha256`

## What happens

Adding a skill from a git repository that uses SHA-256 object format fails before anything is fetched:

```
fatal: mismatched algorithms: client sha1; server sha256
```

Magpie shows it as:

```
git couldn't fetch https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git: fatal: mismatched algorithms: client sha1; server sha256
```

## Environment

- magpie 0.1.3038, macOS 27.0.1, arm64
- `/opt/homebrew/bin/git` 2.56.0 and Apple Git-2.54 (`/usr/bin/git`) both support SHA-256 repositories

## Steps to reproduce

1. `https://gitea.com/gitea/cli` is a SHA-256 repository (every ref from `git ls-remote` is a 64-char hash).
2. In Library, add a skill from `https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/src/branch/main/skills/gt` (or the clone URL `https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git`).
3. Magpie fails with the error above.

## It is not the user's git

Both installed git versions clone the repository fine in a terminal:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git
```

The failure comes from the sequence Magpie runs itself.

## Cause

`internal/library/skillgit.go`, `fetchGit()`:

```go
if _, err := runGit(ctx, git, env, tmp, src, "init", "-q"); err != nil {
    return fail(err)
}
...
if _, err := runGit(ctx, git, env, tmp, src, "fetch", "-q", "--depth", "1", "--no-tags", "--", src.Repo, ref); err != nil {
```

`git init` creates a **SHA-1** repository (the client default), while the remote is **SHA-256**. Git refuses the fetch instead of converting, so every SHA-256 host is unreachable, regardless of the git version.

Reproduced with plain git:

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
git init -q
git fetch --depth 1 --no-tags -- https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git main
# fatal: mismatched algorithms: client sha1; server sha256
```

The same fetch succeeds when the local repository is SHA-256:

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
GIT_DEFAULT_HASH=sha256 git init -q
git fetch --depth 1 --no-tags -- https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git main
git rev-parse --show-object-format   # sha256
```

## Suggested fix

### Option A: let `git clone` negotiate the format

Replace the manual `init` + `fetch` with:

```go
git clone --depth 1 --no-tags -c protocol.ext.allow=never -c core.symlinks=false -- <repo> <tmp>
```

`git clone` reads the remote's `object-format` capability and creates a matching repository, so SHA-1 and SHA-256 hosts both work with no probing. (The existing shallow-fetch fallback for dumb HTTP would still need to be kept.)

### Option B: retry as SHA-256 on that specific error

Keep the current flow, but if the fetch fails with `mismatched algorithms`, recreate the temp repository with the remote's format and retry:

```go
if _, err := runGit(ctx, git, env, tmp, src, "fetch", "-q", "--depth", "1", "--no-tags", "--", src.Repo, ref); err != nil {
    if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(err.Error()), "mismatched algorithms") {
        if err := os.RemoveAll(tmp); err != nil {
            return fail(err)
        }
        if err := os.MkdirAll(tmp, 0o700); err != nil {
            return fail(err)
        }
        if _, err := runGit(ctx, git, env, tmp, src, "init", "-q", "--object-format=sha256"); err != nil {
            return fail(err)
        }
        if _, err := runGit(ctx, git, env, tmp, src, "fetch", "-q", "--depth", "1", "--no-tags", "--", src.Repo, ref); err != nil {
            return fail(err)
        }
    } else if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(err.Error()), "shallow") {
        return fail(err)
    } else if _, err := runGit(ctx, git, env, tmp, src, "fetch", "-q", "--no-tags", "--", src.Repo, ref); err != nil {
        return fail(err)
    }
}
```

`--object-format=sha256` needs git >= 2.29; on older git the retry fails and the original error is still the useful one, so this can be treated as best-effort.

### Related: `hexRef` rejects 64-char hashes

```go
hexRef = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9a-fA-F]{7,40}$`)
```

SHA-256 repositories report 64-char commit ids. `gitRemoteHead()` maps `ls-remote` output through `hexRef`, so for a SHA-256 remote every value is rejected and the head comes back empty (affects update checks, and pinning a skill to a full SHA-256 commit). It should accept up to 64 hex chars.

## Workaround for users

Until this is fixed, mirror the skill into a SHA-1 repository and install from a `file://` URL:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git /tmp/gitea-cli
mkdir -p ~/mirrors/gt-skill
cp -R /tmp/gitea-cli/skills/gt/. ~/mirrors/gt-skill/
cd ~/mirrors/gt-skill
git init -q -b main
git add -A
git -c user.name=mirror -c user.email=mirror@localhost commit -qm "gt skill"
```

Then add `file:///Users/<you>/mirrors/gt-skill` in Library.

issue.title: usage: make allowance charts selectable and card widths adjustable

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
> **Fork review draft:** This PR targets `goubo/magpie`, not `yetone/magpie`. Upstream restricts PR creation to collaborators; GitHub rejected this account's upstream `CreatePullRequest` request. The same branch is available for upstream review at https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...goubo:codex/quota-chart-selection .

## Problem and behavior

Allowance cards currently combine every quota window on one time axis. A five-hour window beside a weekly or monthly window becomes difficult to inspect, and the 260px card minimum leaves little room for long plan names and multiple series. This change lets the reader choose the windows to compare, switch their horizontal alignment, and adjust the overview's card width locally.

### Allowance charts

- Turn the existing legend into multi-select buttons. Initially all windows are selected; only selected windows determine the plotted curves, time range, pace references and pace text. Colors and colorblind patterns keep their original series identity. Deselecting every window leaves the legend available to restore them.
- Add **Use actual time**, on by default. On, selected windows share the real time axis and retain their per-window pace references. Off, each window's complete recorded cycle fills the chart width, with one common full-to-empty diagonal reference and Cycle start / Cycle end labels. Horizontal positions in this mode represent cycle progress; they do not mean that samples occurred at the same timestamp. Sample readings still show their actual times and values.
- Hide the switch when fewer than two legend entries are available, and render actual time in that case. Selecting one of several available entries keeps the switch available. A temporarily hidden switch retains its saved multi-window preference.
- Keep compact charts free of extra ticks and sample readouts. Expanded charts provide percentage labels and exact recorded samples through pointer, touch and keyboard input. Refreshing retains the expanded state within the page.
- Preserve historical snapshot ownership and meters, two-day actual-time behavior, reset gaps and tray/balance calculations. Cycle-progress mode uses the complete recorded cycle even when the global range is two days; switching back restores that actual-time range. A cycle without usable start/reset bounds is omitted with an explanation rather than assigned an invented range.

### Overview layout

- Add a **Layout** popover to the Allowances heading, using the app's existing menu placement and focus behavior.
- Change the default minimum card width from **260px to 360px**. Offer a **280–560px slider in 20px steps**, plus Compact (280), Comfortable (360) and Spacious (440) presets, live preview and the actual column/card-width readout.
- Use the same minimum in the CSS fallback and the JavaScript packer. A container narrower than the preference uses one fitting column; long plan names wrap inside the card. Keep packing order, bottom alignment, chart choices and reading position.
- Handle cold lazy imports without replacing a menu opened later or stealing its focus, and clean up popover observers/listeners when it closes.

## Scope, state and compatibility

The affected subsystem is the [GUI app shell](docs/subsystems/gui-shell.md). Implementation is in [app.js](internal/gui/assets/app.js), [quotacurve.js](internal/gui/assets/quotacurve.js), the [Usage page](internal/gui/assets/plugins/usage/page.js) and its [layout module](internal/gui/assets/plugins/usage/layout.js), with scoped CSS, five-language strings, browser tests and subsystem documentation. The chart interaction and layout controls load lazily to stay within the existing core-script budget; loading the chart module invalidates the packing cache so its final height is measured.

Presentation preferences use existing browser-local storage conventions:

| Key | Value and default |
| --- | --- |
| `magpie.quotaCurveHidden` | Per-account hidden window names, keyed by provider plus normalized account name; absent means all visible. |
| `magpie.quotaCurveRelative` | Accounts using cycle-progress alignment; absent means actual time. |
| `magpie.usageCardMinWidth` | Numeric minimum in pixels; absent/invalid uses 360. Opening the popover alone does not rewrite an invalid stored value. Width changes synchronize between windows. |

There is no server-side preference migration or new dependency. Backend APIs, quota calculation, provider polling, gateway routing, history storage and the database are unchanged. The shared expanded-curve behavior also serves balance charts, so balance and sample-readout regressions are included below.

The larger default can reduce the number of columns and increase page height; the Compact preset provides a denser layout. This is a product layout change and needs maintainer acceptance before merge. All preferences are local to the browser/profile. This PR does not merge, deploy or replace an installed magpie.

## Verification

Tested head: `1a5b0d7803933c772436b526ef7f6a983ae52e17`, rebased on `2f660ca86b1511c624101003fdf66da6ef2c9036`. Tests ran on macOS arm64 with Go 1.27.3 and existing dependencies. Go checks use an isolated temporary HOME, clear agent/MAGPIE/XDG environment overrides, and pin the existing `GOPATH`, `GOMODCACHE` and `GOCACHE`. Browser tests use local fixtures rather than vendor APIs. Linux/Windows results are cross-vet/build checks, not native runtime tests.

| Check | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| 15 relevant browser test files, Chromium + WebKit, five languages, narrow/wide layouts | **237/237 passed**, exit 0. Command below. |
| `node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-concurrency=2 internal/gui/tests/{quota-read-at,balance-curve,balance-currencies}.test.cjs` | **14/14 passed**, exit 0, both engines. |
| `go test -p 2 -tags nogui ./internal/gui -run 'TestCoreScriptBudget\|TestDatesFollowGUILanguage\|TestPurposeAssetMatchesUsage' -count=1 -timeout 5m` | Passed, exit 0; budget was not increased. |
| `go vet -p 2 ./...` | Passed, exit 0, macOS. |
| `GOOS=linux CGO_ENABLED=0 go vet -p 2 -tags nogui ./...` | Passed, exit 0. |
| `GOOS=windows CGO_ENABLED=0 go vet -p 2 ./...` | Passed, exit 0. |
| `go build -p 2 -o <temporary-output> .` | Passed, exit 0; SDK deprecation/linker warnings remain. |
| `GOOS=linux CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -p 2 -tags nogui -o <temporary-output> .` | Passed, exit 0. |
| `GOOS=windows CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -p 2 -o <temporary-output> .` | Passed, exit 0. |
| `go test -p 2 -tags nogui -timeout 45m ./...` | **Failed, exit 1**: 84 packages passed and 3 failed (`internal/agent`, `internal/gateway`, `internal/gui`). Exact failed tests and issue references below. |
| `node --test internal/gui/tests/{i18n-en-no-cjk,i18n-keys}.test.cjs` | **7/8 passed**, exit 1. The failing `a plugin's words are its own` assertion reports the three conflicts listed below. |
| `node --check` on all 13 changed JS/CJS files; `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` | Passed, each exit 0. |
| `gofmt -l` on changed Go files | Not applicable: no Go source changed. |
| Entire GUI suite | **Not run**; the selected files exercise the affected chart, packing, menu, refresh and header paths. Full GUI acceptance remains outstanding before merge. |
| Native Linux/Windows GUI/runtime | **Not run**. |
| GitHub CI | No workflow run or status check was present for this fork branch when inspected; no CI pass is claimed. |
| Native source GUI preview | Previously inspected against the local installed backend from an isolated test configuration. The test GUI has exited and its port has no listener; the installed application was left running. No private account screenshots or logs are uploaded. |

Relevant browser command (using the already installed Playwright runtime):

```sh
node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-concurrency=2 \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-card-width.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-pack.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-arrange.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-quota-head.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-curve-zoom-back.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/quota-curve-selection.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/quota-curve.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/quota-name-wrap.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/quota-window-rows.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/quota-count-wrap.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-card-refresh.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-focus-steady.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-all-accounts.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-phone-head.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/menu-first-second.test.cjs
```

### Tests that fail without the change

- Run the selection regression against original GUI assets: real assertion failure, legend button count **0 instead of 3**.
- Run the card-width regression against original GUI assets: real failure, **“default minimum is 360px, except a narrower container”**.
- Disable per-cycle coordinate mapping in temporary assets: the cycle-progress regression fails.
- Disable the single-entry hiding condition: the regression fails **“one available entry hides the control”**, `true` instead of `false`.

These checks failed through behavior assertions, not compilation or skipped tests. Temporary mutations were removed and the final regressions passed. Existing tests were updated for the new controls, plot-height measurement and explicitly compact packing fixtures. A separate test-only commit fixes a detached-tab race in focus-test setup while retaining every business assertion.

### Outstanding full Go suite

- `internal/agent`: `TestAlmaProvidersSeenDecodeOnce` reports 401 allocations. This single assertion was also independently reproduced on the original unchanged base. No claim is made that this permits shipping; no existing exact-name issue was found by the search.
- `internal/gateway`: `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON`, `TestMarshalSizedIsJSONMarshal` and `FuzzMarshalRaw/seed#7` fail byte/size parity with `encoding/json` for U+2028/U+2029 and invalid UTF-8. Related report: [#5348](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/5348).
- `internal/gateway`: `TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback` says the IPv6 address still answers after the WSL listener closes. [#3680](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3680) explains the probe's reused keep-alive connection and has [a proposed test patch](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/1b93ee5c883344549c48ed1a152d5fe31f431b22). Its full discussion was read; the patch has not been reviewed or ported in this GUI changeset and remains work before merge.
- `internal/gui`: `TestLaneLimitRoutes` receives owner-lane data where it expects an empty object. [#5150](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/5150) explains that a temporary HOME does not isolate `gateway.OwnerLanes()` from its read-only GET to an already running gateway. The test does not need production fallback changed; its owner endpoint needs a controlled fixture. No account/lane payload is published here.

All linked issues and every current comment were read. The non-Alma failures were not independently rerun against this PR's unchanged base, so they are not all labeled baseline failures. No unrelated Go implementation or test assertion was changed to make this feature appear green.

### Outstanding i18n check

`a plugin's words are its own` reports:

- Library: `Use the library's` is also found in `internal/library/skills_shared_copy_test.go`.
- Routing: `No session ID` is also found in `internal/gui/trace.go`.
- Usage: `View routing` is also found in `internal/gui/search_row_archive_test.go`.

These same conflicts were independently reproduced on the original unchanged base. That reproduction does not waive the repository's merge criteria. No unrelated ownership changes are included here.

This remains a **draft**: full-suite failures, unrun GUI/native checks and maintainer approval of the layout/default change must be addressed before merge. A maintainer should recheck the accepted head merged onto current main as required by the code standards.

issue.title: Claude subscription, interactive mode: an effort change restarts the run and rewrites the whole conversation to the cache (#502 for the TUI)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**Version:** magpie 0.1.3216, Claude Code 2.1.318, macOS (arm64). Claude subscription through the gateway, interactive mode on (the default). Client: Pi, on Opus 5.5.

**What happens:** when the effort changes between turns of a conversation, the interactive-mode run is let go and a new Claude Code is started from a replayed transcript. The whole history is written to the prompt cache again. #502 fixed this for `-p` runs (`apply_flag_settings`), but the TUI path still restarts:

```
claude: no run waits for this turn: its run ended 0s ago: its effort is set at its start, and the next turn asks another
claude: a new Claude Code goes on with the conversation from a transcript of it (108 messages, 0 images), typed the last turn's 1
```

**Measured** (from `/v1/magpie/trace`, same session and account, Opus 5.5):

| Turn | Effort | cache_read | cache_write |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| turn before | medium | 88,272 | 762 |
| effort changed (108 messages) | high | 10,858 | 72,416 |
| next turn | high | 83,274 | 1,776 |

Only Claude Code's own system prompt and tools were read from the cache on the changed turn.

A second case on a 148-message conversation with 5 images wrote 178,309 tokens to the cache, and its first token came after 94.4 s. This one request was about two thirds of all Claude cache writes in the trace at that time. Over ~38 h of logs this restart happened 8 times.

**Where:** `serveSubscription` goes on in the same run when the effort changes, except in the TUI:

https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/665b9aff126e26eb5fa8931b7395feb6002185f3/internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go#L1936-L1941

**Why it could stay in the run:** Claude Code 2.1.318's interactive mode has `/effort <level>` (an immediate local command), and Claude Code now sends a mid-conversation effort change per turn, as a `role: "system"` message (the `mid-conversation-system` beta, with a fallback that rewrites the prefix only if the server refuses it). Anthropic's docs say per-message effort on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 "keeps the prompt cache", where a new top-level effort starts it over: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort#change-effort-mid-conversation-beta

The helper already types a local command into the TUI and reads the screen (`/usage`, `internal/claudetui/tui.go`), so there is a path for this.

**Ask:** in an interactive run, type `/effort <level>` before the turn instead of `abortFor`, and keep the run's effort in step. Restart only if Claude Code refuses the level. I haven't tested this through the helper; the evidence is Claude Code's own strings and the docs above.

issue.title: [Performance] Gateway 多个特性在长 Codex 请求体上重复 bytes.Contains 全文扫描

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## 现象

在 Codex / Responses 长上下文请求的 Gateway 转发路径中，多个不同特性都先对整份 `[]byte` 做 `bytes.Contains` 扫描，再按需进行结构化判定或改写。单个检查各自很小，但请求历史不断变长、每轮又要经过多次检查时，会产生可累计的全体字节遍历开销。

这与已有的 #4371（`fastjson.longBody` 反复哈希、验证与顶层 JSON 解析）**不同**：本 Issue 仅追踪各功能预判阶段分散的全文子串搜索，当前 `longBody` 已有 request-scoped 缓存，并不能自动消除它们。

## CPU 证据

2026-11-02 15:45（北京时间） `magpie-cpu-20261102-154550.pb.gz`：

```text
Duration: 30.02s
Total CPU samples: 5.07s (16.89% 单核)

bytes.Contains      0.45s cum (8.88% 全进程)
  -> bytes.Index    0.44s cum

其中来自：
  forVendor.func1                      0.11s cum
  effortUpdated                        0.08s cum
  compactionTriggerIn                   0.05s cum
  (*Server).withoutRefusedPassthrough  0.04s cum
  mayHoldHEIC                           0.04s cum
  mayRefuse                             0.02s cum
  spawnAgentModels                      0.02s cum
  withoutClaudeSeals                    0.02s cum
  其他入口...
```

注意这些数字是函数调用链的 CPU 样本时间（不是调用次数/延迟）；上述子项均已包含在 `bytes.Contains` 路径中，不应累加进总 CPU。此前已有单独的 `hasCustomTool` 全量解码问题 #4892，本 Issue 不重复它。

## 源码举例

1. [codex_backend.go#L3006](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/main/internal/gateway/codex_backend.go#L3006) 的 `forVendor`：
   `slices.ContainsFunc(openaiOnly, func(k []byte) bool { return bytes.Contains(body, k) })`，即对多个 token 标记在 body 上依次搜索，然后又用 `forVendorChanges` 进行结构化检查。
2. [effort_update.go#L247](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/main/internal/gateway/effort_update.go#L247) 的 `effortUpdated` 先进行 `bytes.Contains(body, []byte(`"configuration_update"`))` 再扫描 `input` 的具体 item。
3. [native_compaction.go#L47](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/main/internal/gateway/native_compaction.go#L47) 的 `compactionTriggerIn` 也是先搜索 `"compaction_trigger"` 再检测 `input[].type`。

这些快速预判目前在不命中时可避免更贵的 JSON 解析，**并非应当无条件删除**；改为每次都完整解析可能反而更慢。

## 建议调查/优化

- 为请求生命周期建立便宜、可安全复用的“已发现的顶层字段/功能标记”结果；若已经由 `longBody` / `topMember` / `anyInputItem` 得到结构化信息，可在适当位置传递，而不是每个特性重复全文搜索。
- 重点测量 `forVendor` 对 `openaiOnly` 多个模式的迭代搜索，尝试单遍多模式匹配或利用已有结构化字段判断；只在 benchmark 确认获益时替换预筛选逻辑。
- 路由修改 body 后必须失效或重算相关信息；防止跨请求共享和错误命中。历史文本中恰好含有 `"configuration_update"` 等字符时，不能误判为有效项。
- 避免将所有 feature flag 都强制全量解析；区分常见的直通快路径与需要改写的慢路径。

## 验收

用 64KB / 1MB / 8MB 长历史，分别测“所有标记缺失 / 标记只在聊天文本出现 / 标记真实存在于结构化字段 / 多次 body rewrite”，对比单请求 CPU、`B/op`、`allocs/op`、特性判断结果、上游实际输出。目标是验证在不增加解析/内存开销的情况下减少重复读取的字节数。

原始 Profile 由报告者保留，可按需提供。源码为提交时上游当前状态，采样二进制的准确 commit 尚未确认。此 Issue 是性能优化建议，**不能据此证明任何一个单独扫描是逻辑 bug**。

issue.title: macOS: compact quota rings with live request lights for multiple subscriptions

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Problem and proposal

I use several AI subscriptions at once. Giving each subscription its own logo and figures takes a noticeable amount of menu-bar space. I have used a compact ring layout for a long time in [AI Quota Bar](https://github.com/techfanseric/ai-quota-bar), and would like to offer it as an **optional macOS display mode** in magpie so the subscriptions can be seen together.

I have implemented a first port, including the concurrent-request lights that make the layout useful during work. It is **off by default**; existing numeric mode stays the default.

For the same four synthetic subscriptions, without the bird in either mode, native rendering measures **185 pt → 95 pt** (about 49% narrower). The information tradeoff is intentional: each ring shows the **first selected quota window**, while hover retains the exact figures and all windows.

![Native light/dark numeric and ring comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/techfanseric/magpie/353d74ab441c849cb5edbb33fb0383d2ee1a21ea/comparison.png)

## Activity lights: actual requests and actual destinations

![Native concurrent-request lights](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/techfanseric/magpie/353d74ab441c849cb5edbb33fb0383d2ee1a21ea/live-requests.gif)

The animation demonstrates idle, 1, 2 and 7 upstream requests. One request adds one light, with at most five drawn; hover retains the exact total and model breakdown.

Both previews use synthetic data through the **same native AppKit renderer** as the implementation. They are not recordings of real accounts or an installed production app.

Runtime attribution uses existing magpie state:

- Join `Active.Route` to an unfinished routing `Try` and its matching `Weighed` destination.
- Count only `phase=upstream`, on the actual provider/account/model, including routing-group picks and fallback.
- Deduplicate request IDs; retries do not become extra concurrent work.
- Drop completed/canceled/disappeared requests and reset retained routes when gateway ownership changes.
- Read another local serving process through the existing trace/concurrency APIs; no new HTTP endpoint or response schema.
- On an unreadable peer snapshot, clear old lights and show **Live activity unavailable**, rather than claiming idle.

These are **in-flight model requests, not whole agent tasks**. Local tool execution between requests and requests bypassing magpie cannot be counted this way. I deliberately did not substitute the turn-done quiet-period heuristic for exact request lifecycle data.

The timer runs on the AppKit thread at 12 fps only while visible rings are active. Idle and Reduce Motion modes run no animation timer; Reduce Motion retains stationary lights. Animation frames do not fetch quota or parse trace state. The retained activity map contains destination metadata only, not prompt/reply context.

## Scope

- Settings → Allowances → **Compact quota rings**; local per-computer preference, preserved across older-page/web saves and sync.
- Existing selected cards, account click identities, used/remaining choice and window selection are retained.
- Optional pace is shown as a center reserve/deficit fan.
- Unknown/expired readings and failed readings have distinct symbols; no fabricated fresh 0%/100%.
- Wallet, unlimited/text-only and local token/cost cards retain text.
- Five UI languages. macOS only; Windows/Linux keep their current rendering.
- No new dependency, vendor API, credential storage, routing policy, CI workflow or release-script changes.

## Implementation for review

I am using an Issue because [the contribution policy](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/47b51c8225a66e753dd249cb782472b0dcbee6c4/docs/contributors.md) currently limits PRs to collaborators.

- [Implementation branch](https://github.com/techfanseric/magpie/tree/codex/compact-quota-rings)
- [Commit c1144a85042c02fc16f6adfdcf045b7cc96f25d9](https://github.com/techfanseric/magpie/commit/c1144a85042c02fc16f6adfdcf045b7cc96f25d9) · [applicable patch](https://github.com/techfanseric/magpie/commit/c1144a85042c02fc16f6adfdcf045b7cc96f25d9.patch)
- [User guide, preview reproduction and verification record](https://github.com/techfanseric/magpie/blob/c1144a85042c02fc16f6adfdcf045b7cc96f25d9/docs/compact-quota-rings.md)
- [Owning GUI runtime contract](https://github.com/techfanseric/magpie/blob/c1144a85042c02fc16f6adfdcf045b7cc96f25d9/docs/subsystems/gui-shell.md#compact-quota-rings-on-macos)

Base: `47b51c8225a66e753dd249cb782472b0dcbee6c4`. Preview assets are on a separate asset-only branch, outside the source patch.

## Validation and limits

This implementation is **AI-assisted**. The checks below were executed locally; this is offered for review, not claimed to be ready to merge.

Passed with a temporary HOME and pinned Go caches:

- Focused tray/settings/API/setting-key/core-script-budget tests.
- Relevant race-enabled GUI/gateway/settingsapi checks, including two actual streamed requests through the real gateway HTTP handler to a local fixture upstream: **2 → 1 after canceling one model → 0 when the other finishes**, checking model attribution.
- Native light/dark rendering at 1×/2×/3×, widths, click targets, wave cap and reduced-motion frames.
- **156 related Chromium/WebKit browser tests, 0 failures**; the new ring flow covers all five languages.
- All-package vet/build for macOS, Linux nogui and Windows; gofmt and diff checks. macOS linking emits SDK deployment-target warnings but succeeds.

Deliberately removing wave drawing fails the native motion test; dropping activity counts fails the real-stream test. The new browser flow against actual base assets fails **0 passes / 6 failures** because the control is absent.

**Full `go test -tags nogui ./...` is not green.** Two runs hit gateway affinity/cache failures/timeouts and GUI/library/plugin/netproxy failures. A stricter network-isolated repeat also failed process/provider tests. Related existing reports include #6223, #6249, #6262, #5150, #2562 and #6222. Not all failures were reproduced against the unmodified base; I am not labeling them all as proven baseline failures. The guide records these limits without publishing private machine/account output.

Not run: the entire browser suite, real vendor accounts, an installed Magpie instance with a real profile, or native Windows/Linux runtime checks. Cross-builds are not runtime verification. The full acceptance checks need to pass on current main before merging.

Would this opt-in display be a useful direction for upstream? I am happy to adjust its presentation and scope around the maintainer's preferences.

issue.title: draw and video: a generation request's data URLs are built whole and then copied into the body again

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
draw and video: a generation request's data URLs are built whole and then copied into the body again

## What happens

`picture.dataURL()` (`internal/gateway/draw.go`) builds `"data:" + mediaType + ";base64," + data` for each image a generation request carries — reference images, a mask, a markup image, an edit's input — and its callers in `draw.go`, `draw_*.go`, `video.go` and `video_*.go` put that string straight into the request:

```go
imgs = append(imgs, map[string]string{"url": pic.dataURL(), "type": "image_url"})
req["image"] = d.Images[0].dataURL()
```

Those values go into `map[string]string` (a few into `map[string]any`), so a string is forced, and the request is written by `encoding/json`, which copies each URL into the outgoing body again. One copy of every image is made before it is sent, and a second while it is written.

## Why it matters

It is the same shape as #5748's request-translation path, on the generation path: a full-size intermediate string that the body's writer copies in again. The magnitude is smaller — a generation request carries a handful of images where a translated conversation carries every image of every turn — but a 4 MB reference image is 8 MB on its way out, and an edit or a video request can carry several.

## What is not the same

Nothing in #5748's profile reaches this: it is a different marshaller (`map[string]string` leaves no room for a value type, unlike `marshalBody`'s `jsonSize`/`appendJSONValue`), a different caller (image and video generation, not a translated conversation), and the values are not decoded from a request body, so the held-body sharing rule does not apply.

## A direction

A small value type written straight into the body, the way #5748's `dataURLValue` is, needs a writer that takes it: either `marshalBody` for these requests (they are `map[string]any` in several places already) or a `jsonSize`/`appendJSONValue` case plus a `MarshalJSON` for the `map[string]string` sites, which would have to become `map[string]any` first.

issue.title: gateway: reduce avoidable full-body copies on image turns

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Context

I have been profiling a 20.18 MB image-heavy request through the gateway. `BenchmarkImageRequest/responses-to-chat` currently allocates:

```text
240,465,000 B/op   7,343 allocs/op
```

`BenchmarkImageRequest/messages-to-chat`:

```text
182,219,248 B/op   4,458 allocs/op
```

A `-memprofile` of the request path (excluding the benchmark's own image generation and the fake upstream's `io.ReadAll`) shows the largest avoidable pieces:

```text
60.65 MB  gateway.unquoteJSON
34.45 MB  gateway.readSized
19.41 MB  gateway.dataURL
24.10 MB  gateway.marshalBody
19.25 MB  gateway.ownItems
 4.85 MB  gateway.marshalSized
```

These are mostly copies, not live data the protocol requires.

## Proposal

I have a local prototype with four copy reductions. The first three do not change request acceptance, routing or response shape.

### 1. Read a declared body into one slice up to 64 MiB

`readSized` currently starts at 1 MiB and grows through 1, 2, 4, … MiB, copying the body at each step. For a 20 MiB declared body that is several copies before the body is complete.

A declared body up to 64 MiB can be allocated once at its own size:

```go
first := min(declared, sizedReadFirst)
if declared <= sizedReadOnce { // 64 << 20
    first = declared
}
b := make([]byte, 0, first)
```

Larger declarations keep the 1 MiB first slice so a client cannot make magpie allocate hundreds of MiB by lying about `Content-Length`. Existing tests such as `TestRequestBodyReadOnceAtItsLength` and `TestRequestBodyLengthNotTrusted` cover both sides.

### 2. Share large strings decoded from a held request body

`unquoteJSON` copies a JSON string out of the body. For an image turn, the base64 strings are most of the body, so this copies each picture once more.

The gateway already has `heldBodies` / `inHeldBody`, and `decodeJSON` already shares raw values from a held body. The same rule can apply to large strings:

```go
if share || len(s) >= 1<<20 && inHeldBody(s) {
    return unsafe.String(unsafe.SliceData(s), len(s)), true
}
return string(s), true
```

The threshold keeps small values copied, since a tiny string that shares a large body would keep the whole body alive if retained. Escaped strings still take the existing copy path. The body is already required to be immutable while held (`holdBody`, `checkHeldBody`), so the lifetime rule is the same one raw messages already use.

A test can decode a >1 MiB string from a held body and assert its bytes lie inside the body; a small string from the same body must still be copied.

### 3. Write an image data URL straight into the output JSON

`dataURL(p)` builds `"data:" + mediaType + ";base64," + data`, creating a full-size URL string. `marshalBody` then copies that string into the output body.

A small `imageURLValue` type can be written directly:

```go
dst = append(dst, '"')
dst = appendJSONStringContent(dst, "data:"+mediaType+";base64,")
dst = appendJSONStringContent(dst, data)
dst = append(dst, '"')
```

with matching `jsonSize` and `appendJSONValue` cases, and a `MarshalJSON` fallback for callers that use `encoding/json` directly. This keeps escaping correct, handles non-base64 input, and avoids the intermediate full-size string. Tests compare its bytes with `json.Marshal(dataURL(p))`.

### 4. Share the body of a kept first previous-response turn

`previousResponse` calls `ownItems(fresh)` to copy a turn's items out of the request body so the body can be released. For a first turn whose body is not much larger than its items, an opt-in mode can keep the body and let the kept items point into it:

```go
if !ask.known && len(body) <= own*2 {
    kept = fresh
    // prevTurn keeps the body alive
}
```

The `prevTurn` gains a `body []byte` field, and its `own` accounting uses `len(body)` rather than only the item bytes. Later turns that combine an earlier history still copy the combined list. This trades one full-body copy for retaining the same body until the entry is evicted; it does not retain an extra body.

This one needs the most review because the entry outlives the request. It relies on the same rule the code already states: a request body is not written after it is read. If the maintainers prefer not to keep bodies in the previous-response store, this part can be dropped without affecting the first three.

## Measured result of the prototype

With all four changes, the same benchmarks allocate:

```text
responses-to-chat:  240.5 MB/req -> 98.3 MB/req   (-59.1%)
messages-to-chat:   182.2 MB/req -> 100.6 MB/req  (-44.8%)
large text request:  21.5 MB/req -> 18.7 MB/req   (-12.7%)
```

The remaining allocation is roughly the input body plus the translated output body plus JSON structure. Further reduction would need streaming JSON translation or a raw pass-through path for requests that do not need rewriting; that is a much larger change and is not part of this proposal.

## Questions

- Would a PR along these lines be welcome?
- Are there concerns about extending the existing held-body sharing rule from raw messages to large strings?
- Is retaining `body` in the first previous-response turn acceptable, or should that part stay out of the PR?
- Are there other full-body copies in this path that I missed in the profile?

I can open a PR with the first three changes independently if that is easier to review.

- Remote deployed v0.1.4176: `e0ed2c4d814041c2d3b8ff065ebdd668f7100ba4`.

A response reached its output-token limit with an incomplete function call. Pi rejected execution and serialized its next history with arguments `"{}"`, retaining the call's IDs. Magpie's remote delta discarded that correction and restored the original oversized argument string. The upstream rejected it:

```text
invalid_request_error: input[249].arguments
string_above_max_length: maximum 1048576, actual 4613947
```

The deployed diagnosis comes from versioned source, client serialization checks and correlated redacted logs, not a capture of all HTTP bodies. The deterministic reproduction below uses only synthetic data and fake upstreams.

## Minimal reproduction

Configure gateway B as a Remote Magpie provider of gateway A. Behind B, use a fake Responses upstream.

1. Send A a request with `store:false`, an input array and no `previous_response_id`.
2. Have the fake upstream return this output in `response.incomplete` (also reproducible with a JSON response body):

```json
{"type":"function_call","id":"fc_synthetic","call_id":"call_synthetic","name":"codemode","arguments":"{\"code\":\"unfinished"}
```

3. Send A the original input, then the same output item with `arguments:"{}"`, followed by a `function_call_output` explaining that the truncated call was not executed.
4. Inspect B's request to the fake upstream. It must contain the client's `"{}"`. Before the fix it contains the old incomplete argument string, because A sent only the tail plus `previous_response_id` and B reconstructed its cached output.

The regression generates an incomplete argument string of exactly 4,613,947 ASCII characters to match the observed boundary; no real prompt or tool payload is included. It exercises the existing gateway handler and a second HTTP gateway hop, asserting both the inter-gateway delta decision and the final vendor request. It does not invoke Pi or a real Codex account.

## Root cause and fix

`remoteSentStore.match` hashes the previous input, but `marksMatch` originally compared the previous output only by `type`, `id` and `call_id`. Those IDs survive client corrections. `remoteTurn.delta` then removes the client-supplied output, and the remote's `previousResponse` restores the original output. `prevReply` accepts `response.incomplete` as well as completed responses.

The fix records a bounded SHA-256 content digest beside each output mark. Reuse requires known, matching content as well as the existing ID checks. It reuses `codexSocketItem` normalization for omitted ID/status, nulls, empty lists, annotations/logprobs and key ordering. The relay-added default `final_answer` phase may be omitted; explicit `commentary` remains distinct. Arguments strings, function names, text and other content still count. Cache byte accounting includes the digest and retained strings.

Changed or unreadable content falls back to the client's full history. Unchanged output, including an unchanged incomplete call, still uses delta. The Codex WebSocket transport and incomplete-response caching policy are unchanged.
